attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, stated in the first person.

semantics.note: 'I believe ... is going to' states an unqualified expectation, not a graded hedge, so it is a scored forecast. Treating the capex as AI spending comes from the surrounding context and is reasonable. 'At some point' sets no deadline.

contract.note: Requiring a deliberate cut in overall AI spending, rather than a single project cancellation or timing noise, is the ordinary reading of 'blink and pull back'. With no deadline, continued spending cannot count against him.

evidence.note: Reuters relays an analyst's claim of Microsoft lease cancellations, which Microsoft denied. It does not show a reduction in total AI spending.
Microsoft disclosure projecting higher capex and about $190B for calendar 2026. This is a company-wide figure and cannot rule out a later pullback.
Meta reported Q3 2026 capex of $34.91B and raised the low end of its guidance, so no pullback yet. It cannot contradict an open-ended forecast.
Alphabet's CFO says capex has risen every year and will keep rising. No pullback, but not decisive against an indefinite forecast.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows no company-confirmed cut in total AI infrastructure spending by Google, Microsoft or Meta. The Microsoft lease reports were denied and do not show a net reduction. Rising spending does not refute a forecast with no deadline, so the claim stays open.

attribution.note: He repeats his own earlier words and explicitly reaffirms them ('I was right then and I'm right now').

semantics.note: 'There is no iPhone moment coming' is a firm negative forecast with no deadline. 'I'm afraid' is an idiom, not a hedge.

contract.note: Reading 'iPhone moment' as mass adoption plus a transformative app ecosystem is a fair, ordinary interpretation. A reading based on mass adoption alone could produce a different result, and the contract flags this.

evidence.note: Independent measurement: ChatGPT reached 1B mobile monthly users in May 2026. This shows mass adoption but not the ecosystem part.
OpenAI's own announcement of an apps platform. A launch does not show breadth or lasting use.
Spotify confirms one partner integration. This does not show an ecosystem at transformative scale.

reviews.rationale: Mass adoption is established, but the packet does not show a lasting, independently measured app ecosystem comparable to the iPhone's. The forecast has no deadline, so passing time cannot support it. Neither the contradiction test nor any early-resolution event is met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: A factual description of OpenAI's finances at the time. 'Terrible business' is opinion. The testable parts are the two dollar figures and the claim that there was no proof of cost reduction.

contract.note: Reading 'burn' as cash burn is one choice; the colloquial reading as losses is equally plausible, and the contract flags it. Under the loss reading, $5B would largely match. Requiring annual revenue rather than a run rate is reasonable.

evidence.note: Reports a projected ~$5B loss on $3.7B of 2024 revenue. This is a loss estimate, not cash burn, and the revenue differs from $3.4B.
$3.4B is a June 2024 annualized run rate, not annual revenue, so it measures something different.
OpenAI's own claim that cost per token fell. This is a self-description about prices, not independent evidence of internal production costs.

reviews.rationale: The figures he cites roughly match contemporary reports: ~$5B projected loss, and $3.4B as a run rate against $3.7B projected revenue. But they are different measures from the contract's annual cash burn and annual revenue, and no record of internal costs was found. The packet does not settle the claim as the contract defines it.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Won't' and 'promises to eventually drown' make this a firm forecast with no deadline. 'Better angels' is a concession, not a condition.

contract.note: Reading 'drown' as terminal financial failure, and accepting only durable ad-driven recovery as contradiction, is a fair reading of the metaphor.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure that ads launched in February 2026. This shows exposure to the mechanism, not the outcome, so it is context rather than support.
Secondhand reporting, based on the WSJ, that operating losses grew after ads launched. It does not isolate the effect of ads or show terminal failure.

reviews.rationale: Ads launched and reported losses kept growing, which fits the forecast, but the contract treats interim results as not decisive. Neither terminal failure nor a durable ad-driven recovery appears in the evidence. With no deadline, the forecast stays open.
